subject: Keystone throughput/5xx surge — bridge notes, owner matrix & verification slate
messages:
From: Priya Rao <priya@keystone.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: sre@keystone.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: High latency + 5xx spike on /generate — urgent

Jordan —

We just observed a major performance regression impacting our storefront personalization pipeline. Between 07:05 and 07:30 PDT we saw 99th percentile latencies jump from ~450ms to ~3.1s and a 5xx rate spike to ~2.3% (peak). This is affecting checkout recommendations and we’re seeing a measurable drop in conversion.

I’ve attached a small capture with request ids (support_log_slice_20270914.tar.gz) and a couple of span traces. Can you confirm what changed on your side? Keystone is on a Dedicated pool and we expected autoscaling to handle short bursts. We’re opening an incident on our side as well but need Redwood’s immediate help.

– Priya Rao
Head of Platform Reliability
Keystone Retail

Attachments: support_log_slice_20270914.tar.gz
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@keystone.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 07:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx spike on /generate — urgent

Thanks Priya — we’re live on this. Opening a temporary bridge (Zoom link in thread) and pulling owners: Evelyn (engineer lead) + Marissa (CS lead) for customer comms; Ben for commercial/credits.

Immediate mitigations we’re applying now:
- Force-fallback: divert non-critical traffic to the smaller model variant (m-1) to reduce per-token compute.
- Manual scale-up: spin additional inference replicas in your Dedicated pool + lift concurrency cap for this pool.
- Request-shedding: enable short-term rate-limits on non-essential routes (batch jobs) to prioritise live checkout calls.

We’ll share an initial hypothesis within 30 min and follow with an RCA doc and owner matrix.

Bridge: https://zoom.us/j/000000000 (Keystone + Redwood SREs)

– Jordan Blake
Director, Priority Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priya Rao <priya@keystone.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 07:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx spike on /generate — urgent

Quick technical readout from the bridge:
- Root cause (initial): a kernel selection regression in the 2.4.1 runtime path caused ~+10–15ms per token on the primary model variant. Under a burst of short-lived, high-concurrency requests we hit inefficient batching and excessive kernel context-switching.
- Autoscaler behaviour: the HPA was slow because the burst pattern had many short-lived connections; the default scale-up window under-estimated required replicas.
- KV cache warmup: cold prefixes caused KV-cache misses that amplified tail latency for certain conversation prefixes used by Keystone.

Immediate corrective actions (in-flight):
1) Roll back the kernel path to 2.3.x in the Dedicated pool for Keystone (Evelyn) — ETA 20 minutes.
2) Bump autoscaler aggressiveness and reduce cooldown for this pool (Evelyn/Infra) — ETA 2 hours.
3) Enable prefix-KV pre-warming for high-traffic routes and add a small LRU cache for short-lived keys (Engineering) — ETA 48 hours for staged rollout.
4) Validation: synthetic replay of captured request ids from Priya’s attachment + golden traffic test (QA) — Ben/Marissa to coordinate windows.

I’ll post the rollback job id and logs to the RCA doc once complete.

— Evelyn
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@keystone.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx spike on /generate — customer summary and next checks

Priya —

Thanks for the logs. Short customer-facing summary we plan to send after the rollback and verification:
- What happened: a runtime kernel path regression combined with autoscaler sluggishness and KV-cache cold misses caused brief elevated 99p latency and a measurable 5xx spike.
- Immediate steps taken: forced fallback to smaller model, manual scale-up, rollback of the kernel path, and temporary request-shedding.
- What we’ll do next: tune autoscaler, add KV pre-warming for your hot prefixes, run a 72‑hour stability window, and provide a post-mortem + remediation timeline.

Proposed customer commitments:
- Run enhanced monitoring for 72 hours and provide hourly updates for the first 12 hours.
- Coordinate a controlled replay with your support logs for final verification.
- Apply a one-time service credit for the outage window (Ben will confirm amount with your procurement).

Jordan — if that summary looks good I’ll send it to Priya and their exec chain and attach the RCA v1 when Evelyn posts it.

– Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@keystone.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Keyston e RCA v1, owner matrix and verification plan

Team —

RCA v1 attached (keystone_rca_v1.pdf) and uploaded to drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Keystone-RCA-September-2027
Summary of confirmed fixes and owners:
- Kernel rollback to 2.3.x for Keystone Dedicated pool — Evelyn — DONE (job id: rollback-8721, logs in drive).
- Autoscaler tuning: reduce scale-up cooldown to 20s and add conservative overprovision for short bursts — Evelyn/Infra — ETA 2h (INF-4827).
- KV prefix warming for top-200 prefixes + LRU cache of size 10k — Engineering — Evelyn — ETA 48h (staged).
- Customer replay & verification: Marissa + Ben to schedule a controlled replay window with Keystone SREs — ETA 24h for first validation run.
- Commercial credit: Ben to propose credit amount and contract amendment — Ben — ETA EOD.
- Exec readout: Jordan/Marissa to deliver a short executive note to Keystone leadership after the 72-hour stability window.

Validation plan (high-level):
1) Immediate smoke tests (30m after rollback) — pass.
2) Golden traffic replay (within 24h) against tuned pool — verify 99p under 600ms.
3) 72-hour monitored window with hourly checks then daily summary for 7 days.

Attachments: keystone_rca_v1.pdf, autoscaler_config_before_after.diff

Jordan Blake
Director, Priority Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Rao <priya@keystone.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, sre@keystone.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Keyston e RCA v1, owner matrix and verification plan

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the quick response and for the clear owner matrix. We saw immediate improvement after the rollback; 99p dropped back below 550ms in our initial smoke checks. We’ll run the controlled replay tomorrow morning (08:00 PDT) and will report back with the full trace set.

Please proceed with the autoscaler tuning and KV warming plan. We’ll expect the exec readout after the 72-hour stability window. Also confirm the credit amount and timeline for the contract amendment.

Appreciate everyone moving fast on this.

– Priya
Head of Platform Reliability
Keystone Retail
